title: Large Language Models meet Collaborative Filtering: An Efficient All-round LLM-based Recommender System

problem.claim: Collaborative filtering recommender systems struggle in cold scenarios with sparse user-item interactions.

gap.claim: Methods leveraging user/item modality information and pretrained modality encoders or LLMs can underperform traditional collaborative filtering models in warm scenarios because they lack collaborative knowledge.

contributions.claim: The authors propose A-LLMRec, an LLM-based recommender system intended to perform in both cold and warm scenarios.

A-LLMRec enables an LLM to use collaborative knowledge from a pretrained state-of-the-art collaborative filtering recommender, jointly exploiting the LLM's emergent ability and pretrained user/item embeddings.
The approach extends beyond recommendation to natural-language generation through favorite genre prediction based on collaborative knowledge.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that A-LLMRec is model-agnostic and can integrate with various existing collaborative filtering recommenders.
The authors report improved efficiency by eliminating the extensive fine-tuning typically required for LLM-based recommenders.
Experiments on various real-world datasets are reported to demonstrate superiority across cold/warm, few-shot, cold-user, and cross-domain scenarios.

narrative_sequence.summary: Collaborative filtering has improved user experience in social media and e-commerce recommendation settings.
Sparse interactions create difficulty in cold scenarios, motivating the use of modality information, pretrained modality encoders, and LLMs.
These approaches may lose collaborative knowledge and underperform traditional collaborative filtering in warm scenarios.
A-LLMRec connects an LLM with collaborative knowledge and pretrained embeddings from a state-of-the-art collaborative filtering recommender.
The authors report broad scenario results and demonstrate natural-language generation through favorite genre prediction.

unknowns: No quantitative results, dataset names, metrics, or baseline comparisons are provided.
The mechanism for exposing collaborative knowledge and the required training procedure are unspecified.
The scope and conditions of the reported efficiency gains are unspecified.
No details are provided for the favorite genre prediction task or natural-language evaluation.
